newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat lobby wants bigger EU export priority.
newsitem.headline: French wheat lobby wants bigger EU export priority.

text.p: A senior French wheat growers' representative urged the European Commission on Monday to reconsider its policy of tailoring exports to internal prices.
Jean-Jacques Vorimore, number two at the AGPB wheat growers' lobby, also called on the Commission to start exporting quickly now that a controversial wheat export tax has been dropped.
"There are people at the Commission who want to wait before exporting and who are saying that if we export too early on the world market, then internal prices will rise," Vorimore said.
"This is an aberration," he added, speaking to Reuters on the eve of an AGPB annual gathering in Dijon, eastern France.
"We ask that Europe's export policy should not be solely geared towards the internal market but to both internal and export markets," he said.
His remarks reflect growing debate about an issue which has increasingly put farmer against farmer in the past year.

Export-oriented farmers and major grain users like livestock breeders or feed manufacturers are feuding for control over grain policy, amid fears inside the Commission that past reforms meant to reduce local prices could suffer if exports come first.
Internal prices flew up with an explosion of world markets last April but have not fully relaxed since, partly because of low grain stocks and steadily rising demand for animal feed.
The Commission, acting on political instructions from EU ministers, has repeatedly said its task is to protect the 1992 reforms by ensuring affordable local supplies before exporting.
Vorimore, who is the AGPB's secretary general and heads the EU's outside consultative group on grain, said staying off world markets would play into the hands of the United States.
"We must not wait before positioning ourselves on the world market as we did last year. It would be an error," he said.
"Brussels should resume exports as soon as possible. As soon as there is a market, let's go," he said.
EU officials have said they plan to open up a series of export tenders for the 1997/98 (July/June) campaign but they are in no hurry to award export subsidies under the tender system.

However, they say last season's campaign, which officially runs until June 30 but effectively ended in April, saw steady sales in the second half of the season. This led to a 50 percent jump in exports in one year to 9.8 million tonnes.
Wheat exports were certain to be on the agenda for talks between EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman in Washington on Monday.

But the EU's decision to abolish its wheat export tax last week has eased a key source of friction between world exporters. Analysts say scrapping the tax was a first step towards resuming stalled wheat exports, and although this will rival U.S. wheat it will please a U.S. administration which is concerned about sending out wrong signals to importers.
